dimensions.assessment: Affects taxpayers in states, territories, and the District of Columbia affected by natural disasters, fires, floods, or explosions.
dimensions.evidence: taxpayers affected by a qualified state declared disaster, upon written request by the state governor

dimensions.assessment: Provides administrative relief by extending tax filing and payment deadlines and allowing state-level disaster coordination.
dimensions.evidence: increases the automatic extension of federal tax deadlines for these taxpayers to 120 days (from 60 days)

dimensions.assessment: Temporarily defers the timing of federal tax collections during qualifying disasters without altering tax rates or permanent revenue.
dimensions.evidence: postpone federal tax deadlines for taxpayers affected by a qualified state declared disaster

dimensions.assessment: Modifies Section 7508A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 regarding disaster tax relief authority and automatic extensions.
dimensions.evidence: amends by redesignating subsections... and by inserting after subsection (b) the following new subsection

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent changes to federal tax code disaster relief procedures for future declarations.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by this section shall apply to declarations made after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Specific estimates of the number of taxpayers who will utilize state-declared disaster extensions annually.
importance_detail.rationale: This enacted law authorizes the IRS to postpone federal tax deadlines upon written governor request for state-declared disasters and extends automatic tax relief deadlines from 60 to 120 days for eligible disaster victims and relief workers.
